h1: The 6 Best Egg Cookers With Timers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Egg Cookers With Timers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 egg cookers with timers compared on capacity, digital controls, auto shut-off, poaching and omelet trays and cleanup.
summary: The Elite Gourmet 6-Egg Digital cooker is the best pick for most kitchens, with preset menus, a mutable beeper and poached and omelet modes. The SUSTEAS cooks up to nine eggs in three zones with a 24-hour timer, the Dash is the simple chime-on-done choice, and the Tesslux lets you set exact minutes on a touch panel.
intro: Egg cookers sell on promise of effortless, but the real work is the water. Most of these steam eggs from a measured cup of water, and the line on the measuring cup is the doneness dial. A cooker that makes you guess at the water or the time is no easier than a pot. Timers and presets are worth buying only if they take the guessing out.

We ranked six egg cookers from the listings: capacity, controls, timer type, auto shut-off, extra trays and cleanup. Capacities run from 6 to 9 eggs, and the controls from a single switch to a touch panel. A good cooker shuts off by itself, which protects the plate if the water runs out, and signals when it is done.

products.name: Elite Gourmet 6-Egg Digital Egg Cooker
products.verdict: A 6-egg digital cooker with preset menus, a mutable beeper and poached and omelet modes.
products.description:
The Elite Gourmet is a 6-egg cooker with a digital preset menu, a one-touch graphic display, a mutable beeper and poached and omelet modes.

It ranks first because presets take the water math out of the job, and a beeper you can mute means a quiet kitchen at dawn. It beats the Dash on controls, since the Dash is a plain switch. The six-egg capacity is smaller than the SUSTEAS's nine.

Buy it if you want presets and a quiet timer. Skip it if you cook for a large family. Its mutable beeper is the detail most families end up valuing.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want preset modes without water math.

products.name: SUSTEAS Rapid Egg Cooker 9 Eggs
products.verdict: A 9-egg cooker with 3-zone cooking, a 24-hour timer, auto shut-off and dry-burning protection.
products.description:
The SUSTEAS cooks up to nine eggs across three zones of three eggs each, with a 24-hour timer, auto shut-off and dry-burning protection.

It ranks second because three zones let you cook different doneness in one batch, which is the best feature for families or meal prep. It loses to the Elite Gourmet on presets and a muteable beeper. The 24-hour timer is a delay feature, not a cooking time.

Buy it if you cook many eggs in mixed doneness. Skip it if you cook only a couple. Its zones also let you cook a mix of runny and hard eggs at once.
products.idealFor: Families or meal preppers cooking up to nine eggs.
products.skipIf: You only cook a few eggs.

products.name: Tesslux Electric Egg Cooker 6-Egg
products.verdict: A 6-egg cooker with an 800W plate, a touch panel with plus and minus and five egg styles.
products.description:
The Tesslux has a 6-egg capacity, an 800W heating element, a touch panel with plus and minus keys, a non-stick heating plate and five egg styles.

It ranks third because the plus and minus keys let you set exact minutes, which presets cannot. It costs $25-50 and has the same capacity as the Elite Gourmet. A touch panel is easy to wipe but can be fussy with wet fingers.

Buy it if you want exact control over minutes. Skip it if you want one-touch presets. Exact minutes help when you swap between soft and hard on the same morning.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want to set exact minutes.

products.name: Dash Rapid Egg Cooker 7 Eggs
products.verdict: A 7-egg cooker with a poaching tray, an omelette bowl, a thermal sensor shut-off and a chime.
products.description:
The Dash Rapid cooker holds seven eggs, comes with a poaching tray and an omelette bowl, shuts off with a thermal sensor and chimes when done.

It ranks fourth because it is a one-switch design at the under $25 bracket, which is simple but gives no timer. It beats the Amazon Basics on extras, since it includes poaching and omelet trays.

Buy it if you want a simple switch and a chime. Skip it if you want a timer to set. Pair it with a measuring cup that is easy to read.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants a simple switch and a chime.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Egg Cooker 7-Egg
products.verdict: A 1.4 lb seven-egg cooker with auto shut-off and dishwasher-safe parts.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics cooker holds seven eggs, weighs 1.4 pounds, shuts off automatically and has dishwasher-safe, BPA-free parts.

It ranks fifth because dishwasher-safe parts take the cleanup off your hands, but the listing offers no timer and fewer extras than the Dash. It is under $25.

Buy it if you want light and easy to clean. Skip it if you want poaching trays or a timer. Dishwasher cleanup is the quiet advantage that keeps it in use.
products.idealFor: Small kitchens that want a light, dishwasher-friendly cooker.

products.name: Evoloop Rapid Egg Cooker 6 Eggs
products.verdict: A 6-egg cooker about 7.6 inches tall, with a poacher and omelet maker.
products.description:
The Evoloop holds six eggs in a small body, roughly 7.6 inches high on an 5.6 by 8.6 inch base, and includes a poacher and an omelet maker.

It ranks last because the listing gives no timer, shut-off or wattage details. The small footprint is its strength.

Buy it if you travel or have a small kitchen. Skip it if you want listed timer features. Its small size suits a dorm, an office or a camper.

whatMatters.detail: Presets set the cook time for soft, medium or hard, and some cookers let you key minutes. Check the controls on the listing, and decide whether you want presets or manual minutes. Presets take the guessing out of soft, medium and hard, while manual minutes suit cooks who already know their timing, so pick the style that matches your habits.

Six, seven and nine eggs are the sizes here. A larger cooker takes more room. Check the capacity on the listing, and the zone layout if you want mixed doneness. A big cooker is wasted on two eggs and a small one means two batches for a family, so buy for the number you cook most mornings.

The cooker stops when the water boils off, which protects the plate. Look for auto shut-off, thermal sensor or dry-burn protection on the listing. Water boiling off is the hazard in any steam cooker, which is why auto shut-off or dry-burn protection earns its place on a listing.

Poaching trays and omelet bowls turn an egg cooker into a small breakfast station. Check what is in the box. An omelet bowl or poaching tray costs little but widens what the cooker does, so check whether they are in the box.

Non-stick plates and dishwasher-safe parts make cleanup quick. Look for these on the listing, and rinse the plate to avoid scale. Mineral scale builds on the plate over months, so a non-stick surface and a vinegar rinse keep it working.

faq.a: Yes. Most steam eggs from a measured cup of water, and the cup's lines set doneness. The Dash and Amazon Basics use that method. A fresh measuring cup line gives repeatable results.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Measuring the water wrong. The water level sets doneness, so use the measuring cup that comes with the Elite Gourmet or Dash and fill to the right line. Large cookers suit batches of boiled eggs for the week.

faq.q: Is the SUSTEAS worth it over the Elite Gourmet?
faq.a: For batches, yes. The SUSTEAS cooks nine eggs in three zones, while the Elite Gourmet has presets and a mutable beeper. A quiet beeper helps in a sleeping house.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Add water to the line, place eggs on the tray, close the lid and start. The Tesslux needs minutes set on its panel. Plan to descale every month in hard water.

faq.q: How do I look after one?
faq.a: Descale the plate with vinegar and water, and wash trays by hand or in the dishwasher on the Amazon Basics. Poaching works best with fresh eggs.

faq.q: Can I cook something besides eggs?
faq.a: The Dash and Elite Gourmet include omelet and poach trays, so you can make small omelets and poached eggs. Keep the cord clear of the hot plate.

finalTake: The Elite Gourmet 6-Egg Digital Egg Cooker is the best buy, with presets, a mutable beeper and poached and omelet modes. The SUSTEAS is the big-batch cooker, the Tesslux is for exact minutes, and the Dash is the simplest chime. Measure the water carefully.
